plan.question: Why did narrowing the airbench96 net from 128/384/576 to 128/256/384 and raising epochs from 8.5 to 12 reach only 74.56% on CIFAR-100 (E009), when our models predicted 74.9-76.1%? E007 suggests the narrow net gains only about +0.5 pp from 10 to 12 epochs plus lighter regularization, while the wide net reaches 75.5% in 8.5 epochs. What mechanism makes narrow CNNs gain little from extra epochs in short-budget, many-class training? Candidates are a width-limited capacity or accuracy ceiling, wider nets being more sample efficient per step, a too-narrow final feature dimension for 100 classes, or LR/weight-decay settings that don't transfer across widths. Given those, is there a width/epoch trade-off (or an intermediate width such as 128/320/480 with a wide final stage) that beats the wide net's time?

rubric: Measures accuracy as a joint function of model width (or parameters) and training steps/epochs under a fixed compute or time budget, ideally in a short or under-trained regime

Reports results on CIFAR-100 or another many-class image dataset with CNNs/ResNets, or gives a mechanism (capacity ceiling, sample efficiency vs width, feature-dimension bottleneck) that transfers to them
Gives quantitative guidance usable for choosing per-stage widths or epochs, such as scaling exponents, an optimal width-to-steps ratio, or which stage's width matters most
Or shows how optimal LR/weight decay/momentum shift with width, explaining why fixed hyperparameters underperform on narrower nets
exclude: Pretrained weights, transfer learning, fine-tuning or distillation from external/pretrained teachers
External or extra training data, synthetic data generation from outside models
Test-time augmentation or any use of the test set during training
Large-scale language-model-only scaling studies with no transferable CNN mechanism
Pruning/compression of already-trained models for inference speed only
